title: Top pay where the City is the main funder
question: Where does the highest-paid person earn more than a City department head on mostly City money, and where did top pay climb while the organization shrank?
finding: 30 organizations qualify: 16 that get at least a quarter of their revenue from the City raised their top earner’s pay by at least a fifth while revenue or the number of people served fell, and 14 pay their top earner more than the typical City department head ($273,274 in fiscal 2025) while drawing at least half their revenue from the City.
how: The highest total (pay from the organization plus related organizations) on each return’s Part VII, earliest return against latest (at least two years apart); revenue from Part I; City share is City payments in the matching fiscal year divided by total revenue; stated service counts are those already extracted from the returns’ program descriptions. The department-head figure is the median salary of full-year “Dept Head” jobs in the fiscal 2025 payroll.
limits: Pay is set by each board and no rule caps it. The top earner can be a different person in the two years, a physician rather than the executive, or include a one-time payout. City payments can exceed a year’s reported revenue when timing differs. Stated counts are text-mined and can change definition between years.
